claims.text: The as-manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a homogeneous FCC matrix.
The as-manufactured alloy exhibits high strength and fatigue performance.
Elevated-temperature degradation is governed by environment-dependent evolution of the surface oxide scale.
In oxidizing atmospheres, Cr and Al oxidize rapidly and selectively.
Selective oxidation of Cr and Al produces a continuous, adherent protective oxide scale.
The continuous Cr- and Al-derived oxide scale limits oxygen ingress into the underlying FCC matrix.
Reducing atmospheres suppress or destabilize formation of a robust surface oxide scale.
The absence or instability of a robust oxide scale under reducing conditions permits inward oxygen diffusion.
Inward oxygen diffusion under reducing conditions causes internal oxidation, particularly of Ti.
Internal oxidation under reducing conditions is concentrated along grain boundaries.
Oxidizing exposure will produce a thin, uniform, adherent oxide layer with minimal internal oxidation.
Mechanical properties will be preserved after oxidizing exposure.
Reducing exposure will produce a less continuous oxide scale than oxidizing exposure.
Reducing exposure will cause more measurable grain-boundary internal oxidation than oxidizing exposure.
Internal oxidation under reducing exposure will reduce tensile strength and fatigue performance relative to the as-manufactured baseline.
The proposed degradation mechanism applies over approximately 700–900 °C when exposure is long enough to produce observable oxidation.
Conditions outside 700–900 °C may activate different degradation mechanisms.
